findings.where: apps/web/lib/clara/intentKey.ts:64-68 (canonicalIntentAddress) + apps/web/lib/clara/useClaraThread.ts:418 (the derive call) + packages/db/migrations/0006_runtime_core.sql:954-960 (the unbounded replay lookup)
findings.what: The turn key is addressed by (threadId, altitude, trimmed draft, sorted attachment ids) and NOTHING that advances with the conversation. Every REPEATED utterance in a session therefore derives the key of the FIRST one and lands on begin_chat_turn's replay branch, which returns the original task without ever reading p_user_parts. The second message is silently dropped: no bubble, no task, no run, no Work, no error — the composer clears and a status line says 'Clara already had that message'. In an agent chat the repeated utterance IS the common case ('yes', 'ok', 'continue', 'post it', re-asking 'show me the trial balance'). The lookup has no time or state bound (0006:955-960, `limit 1`, no ordering, no window; chat_messages is append-only), so the collapse is PERMANENT for the life of the session — the person can never send that sentence again and must reword to be heard. This is a regression the branch introduces: before it, useClaraThread.ts minted crypto.randomUUID() per press and every genuine repeat was admitted.
findings.evidence: MEASURED with a throwaway red cell in the branch's own harness (apps/web/components/clara/thread-intent-key.test.tsx copied verbatim; file written, run, deleted; worktree left clean). PROBE1 drove the REAL send path twice with 'yes', the first send accepted and SETTLED (event: done) and the composer cleared, then 'yes' retyped: the wire carried `["intent-7cd79e5c858fe0c3f74622eac6a9deeb","intent-7cd79e5c858fe0c3f74622eac6a9deeb"]` — byte-identical keys — and the product's entire response to the second message was the single status line `Clara already had that message — this is the same request, not a second one.` CORROBORATED BY THE BRANCH'S OWN DB EVIDENCE: packages/runtime/tests/chat-turn-replay-db.test.mjs:130-160 (`p642.runtime.turn_replay_after_terminal`) asserts that after the first turn SETTLES a same-key POST answers 202 with the original terminal task, `tasks.rows[0].n === 1` (no second task), `rows.length === 1` (no second user row) and `clara.accounting_work gained no second row` — i.e. the worker measured the swallow and shipped it as the acceptance criterion. packages/db/tests/rig-runtime-lifecycle.test.mjs:527-530 measures the same at the door: the surviving row carries the FIRST payload. apps/web/e2e/chat-parity-walk.spec.ts:667-675 enshrines it in the browser walk.
findings.fix: Add the conversation's POSITION to the address — one more length-prefixed field in canonicalIntentAddress (apps/web/lib/clara/intentKey.ts:66), e.g. the count or last id of the persisted messages the composer has seen (`state.messages.length` / the last MessageRow id, both already in the store). Retry semantics are preserved exactly: a refused or lost send adds nothing to the transcript, so the retry derives the SAME key (including after a reload, since the transcript is re-read to the same length); a re-typed identical message AFTER a settled turn sees a longer transcript and derives a NEW key. Everything the branch's cells assert (p642.web.intent_key_survives_a_refusal, intent_key_and_changed_attachments, e2e.duplicate_send with the ack dropped mid-turn) stays green, because in every one of those the transcript has not advanced.

findings.what: The two NEW role="status" lines are gated only on `!revoked`; they are NOT part of the file's mutually exclusive status ladder. The replayed line and the stream-status line therefore announce SIMULTANEOUSLY for one press, which is exactly the defect class this file's own comments say was fixed twice (:577-581 'two role="status" siblings would announce twice', :592-595 'without that gate "Clara is responding…" and this line were two live regions announcing one press', :618-620 'it is exclusive with the other two above for the same reason they are exclusive with each other'). `checkingBeforeSend` can likewise coexist with `runLostSight` (:621), since neither gates on the other. The nested-live-region gate (thread-live-tool-states.test.tsx:171) does not catch this — it counts NESTING, not simultaneity — and thread-revoked.test.tsx:117's `lines.length === 1` is only asserted on the revoked arm, where everything else IS gated.
findings.evidence: MEASURED (same throwaway harness, PROBE2): beginSend → markAccepted(thread, task, replayed=true) → one `text-delta` chunk, then every role="status" node in the rendered tree collected: `["Clara already had that message — this is the same request, not a second one.","Clara is responding…"]` — 2 lines, assertion `2 !== 1`. This is the ordinary replay path: a replayed task that is still running streams chunks immediately, so both lines are on screen for the whole turn.
findings.fix: Fold both new lines into the existing exclusive ladder — add `&& !stopped && stopFailedCause === null && !runLostSight && !streamStatusLabel(state, t)` to :565 and :571, or (better) render `alreadyAccepted` as plain non-live text: it is a fact about the SEND, not a live transition, and it does not need to be announced twice beside 'Clara is responding…'. Pin it with a cell that counts role="status" nodes on the replayed+streaming state, the shape thread-revoked.test.tsx:117 already uses.

findings.where: apps/web/lib/clara/threadStore.ts:300 (the only writer of `lastSendReplayed: true`) and :266 (the only clear, inside `beginSend`); rendered at apps/web/components/clara/ClaraThreadView.tsx:565
findings.what: `lastSendReplayed` is cleared by NOTHING except the next `beginSend`. `applyStreamEvent` (threadStore.ts:368-381), `markSendFailed` (:350-360), `markSent` (:347), `hydrateRun` and `hydrateMessages` all leave it set, and `useClaraThread`'s `[threadId]` effect (useClaraThread.ts:274-280) clears `lastIntentKeyRef` but not this store flag. The store is module-level and survives unmount, so after a replayed send the line 'Clara already had that message — this is the same request, not a second one.' stays on screen through the whole turn, after it settles, and across a rail close/reopen — a sentence about a press nobody is looking at any more, sitting over a quiet transcript. The field's own doc comment (:57-62) says 'the surface says it ONCE', which is not what the lifetime delivers.
findings.evidence: Code, exhaustively: `grep -n lastSendReplayed apps/web/lib/clara/threadStore.ts apps/web/components/clara/ClaraThreadView.tsx` returns exactly five sites — the interface (:62), the empty state (:93), the clear in beginSend (:266), the set in markAccepted (:300) and the render (ClaraThreadView.tsx:565). No mount/unmount/settle/thread-change path touches it. Module-level persistence is the same property thread-rehydrate.test.tsx relies on.
findings.fix: Clear it on the terminal the same way `settled`/`revoked` retire the clock in threadStore.ts:368-381, or give it the `markSent` transition — one line beside the existing `pendingUserParts` write.

findings.where: apps/web/lib/clara/useClaraThread.ts:257 (`lastIntentKeyRef` is a per-MOUNT useRef), :278 (reset to null) and :433 (`priorKey !== null` in the pre-read condition)
findings.what: The DISTINCT-resubmit pre-read — appendix C §3's left column, the thing cell p642.web.distinct_resubmit_reads_state_first exists to deliver — is keyed on a ref that lives only as long as the mount, while the `sendStatus === "error"` it pairs with lives in the module-level store. After a rail close/reopen, a scope switch back, or any remount following a failed send, `priorKey` is null, the `priorKey !== null` conjunct is false, and a genuinely DIFFERENT intent posts with no state re-read at all — the exact case the brief says nothing else protects (a different key cannot reach the door's replay branch).
findings.evidence: MEASURED (same throwaway harness, PROBE3): send 'book the invoice from Rome' → 500 → `claraThreadStore.getThread(THREAD).sendStatus === "error"`; unmount; remount; send the DIFFERENT sentence 'actually, book the Milan one'. Transcript reads before/after the distinct resubmit: **2 → 2** (no pre-read), with the new mount still observing `sendStatus: "error"`. The branch's own cell (apps/web/components/clara/thread-intent-key.test.tsx:207-240) only exercises the single-mount path, so it stays green.
findings.fix: Put the last posted key on the thread's store state beside `lastSendReplayed` (threadStore.ts) instead of in a mount-scoped ref, or treat `outcomeUnknown && priorKey === null` as 'unknown and unattributable' and take the pre-read.

findings.where: packages/runtime/src/streamRoute.ts:31-44 (attach-time AuthError answers an HTTP status, never an SSE `revoked`) vs :152-157 (the mid-stream arm the branch consumes); apps/web/lib/clara/stream.ts:329
findings.what: AC5's `revoked` hole is only half closed. A revocation discovered at ATTACH time — the reattach after a `detached`, a rail reopen, a scope switch back, any remount while the membership is already gone — comes back as HTTP 403/404, which `openTaskStream` turns into `throw new Error('stream attach failed (403)')` (stream.ts:329). That takes the ordinary reconnect path: backoff 1s→2s→4s→…, up to `maxAttempts: 8` (~3 minutes of 'Reconnecting… (attempt N)'), then a generic give-up. The person who has lost access is still told the connection is flaky, never that their access was removed — the same sentence the ticket set out to retire, on a path the new `case "revoked"` never sees.
findings.evidence: Code, both ends: streamRoute.ts:37-41 returns `res.status(err.status).json(...)` for an AuthError before any SSE header is written (`res.status(200).set({Content-Type: text/event-stream})` is at :48-53, after it), so no `revoked` frame can exist on that path; stream.ts:329 throws a plain Error on `!res.ok`, and `runClaraTaskStream`'s new arm (stream.ts:459-467) only inspects `evt.event`, which requires a frame. DEFAULT_RECONNECT_POLICY at stream.ts:353-358.
findings.fix: In `openTaskStream`/`runClaraTaskStream`'s attach-failure arm, treat 401/403/404 as the terminal revocation rather than a reconnectable transport failure — deliver the same `{event:'revoked', data:{taskId, reason}}` the mid-stream arm delivers, so one fact has one face. One cell, the shape of stream-revoked.test.ts:65.

findings.what: The composer is marked `aria-invalid` when a send fails, but nothing accessible says WHY: `aria-describedby` names only the static Enter/Shift+Enter hint, and the send error renders as a `StateBanner` elsewhere in the tree that the field never references. `FieldError` is not imported (:23 imports `Field, FieldDescription, FieldGroup, FieldLabel` only), although the brief's slice item 6 and cell 15 both name it. A screen-reader user hears 'invalid' with no reason and no route to one.
findings.evidence: ClaraThreadView.tsx:23 (`import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field"` — no FieldError), :779, :783; the branch's own cell apps/web/components/clara/composer-field-wiring.test.tsx:146 asserts only that the attribute appears and the draft survives, never that the invalid state is described.
findings.fix: Render the send error as a `FieldError` inside the `Field` and append its id to `aria-describedby` while invalid — the `work-question-form.tsx:70` shape the brief points at already does this.

findings.what: The scroll hook's `revision` is a SUM of five independent lengths, so two opposite changes landing in one commit cancel and the append effect (useTranscriptScroll.ts:208-219) does not run: the reader at the bottom is not followed and the reader scrolled up is not re-offered the jump control. The narrow but real case is the provisional bubble retiring (−1) in the same commit as one arriving chunk (+1), which is precisely what `markSent`/the first chunk do together.
findings.evidence: ClaraThreadView.tsx:287-292 (`state.messages.length + state.stream.provisionalChunks.length + (state.pendingUserParts ? 1 : 0) + clarifyParts.length + liveToolSteps.length`); useTranscriptScroll.ts:219 (`[revision, viewport, publishAtBottom, publishHasMoreBelow]`). Not measured — the collision is a single-commit coincidence I did not force.
findings.fix: Make the revision a monotonic counter bumped on any content change, or a cheap composite string, rather than a sum that can be stationary across a real change.

findings.what: `done`, `failed` and `refused` all rank 2 and the comparison is strict, so once a call id reaches any of them no later chunk can change it. A `tool-error` arriving after a `tool-result` for the same `toolCallId` would leave the chip reading *done* for a step that threw. Whether the AI SDK can emit both for one call is documented-not-measured (the header at :14-29 measured the FIELD NAMES, not the ordering), so this is a note rather than a defect.
findings.evidence: liveTools.ts:66, :116. The branch's cells (apps/web/lib/clara/liveTools.test.ts:54-67, :118-127) drive result-then-nothing and a replay from index 0, never error-after-result.
findings.fix: If the ordering is possible, give `failed` a rank above `done`/`refused` (a thrown tool is the stronger statement), or key the terminal arm on last-writer-wins for the three rank-2 states only.

findings.what: Two document-global literal ids on a component that is mounted from two different places (the rail via rail-mount.tsx and the escalated `(full)` routes). Today only one instance is ever mounted at a time, so nothing breaks; the moment a second one is (a split view, a preview, a test that renders both variants), the label/description association silently binds to the first and the second composer loses its accessible name.
findings.fix: `useId()` and interpolate, which is what `@/components/ui/field`'s own primitives expect.
